'''''Ranunculus trichophyllus''''', the '''threadleaf crowfoot''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=RATR|taxon=Ranunculus trichophyllus|accessdate=18 October 2015}}</ref> or '''thread-leaved water-crowfoot''',<ref name="BSBI07">{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17 }}</ref><ref name="RHS">{{cite web |title=Ranunculus trichophyllus |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/14378/Ranunculus-trichophyllus/Details |publisher=rhs.org.uk |access-date=27 October 2017}}</ref> is a plant species in the genus ''[[Ranunculus]]'', native to [[Europe]], [[Asia]] and North America.

It is a [[herbaceous]] [[annual plant|annual]] or [[perennial plant]] generally found in slow flowing streams, ponds, or lakes. The daisy-like [[flower]]s are white with a yellow centre, with five petals.<ref name="Readers">{{cite book |year=1981 |title=Reader's Digest Field Guide to the Wild Flowers of Britain |page=30 |publisher=[[Reader's Digest]] |isbn=978-0-276-00217-5}}</ref>
It is similar in form to ''[[Ranunculus fluitans]]'' (river water-crowfoot), apart from flower petal number, thread-leaved has on 5 petals and shorter leaves, as thread-leaved prefers slower flowing waters. It also has rounded seed heads which become fruits covered with bristles.<ref name="Readers" />
The segmented leaves and the plants ability to [[photosynthesis]] underwater have been studied.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Rascio|first1=N.|last2=Cuccato|first2=F.|last3=Dalla Vecchia|first3=F.|last4=La Rocca|first4=N.|last5=Larcher|first5=W.|title=Structural and functional features of the leaves of Ranunculus trichophyllus Chaix., a freshwater submerged macrophophyte|journal=Plant, Cell and Environment|date=February 1999|volume=22|issue=2|pages=205–212|doi=10.1046/j.1365-3040.1999.00394.x|bibcode=1999PCEnv..22..205R |doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
It was first described and published by the French naturalist and botanist [[Dominique Villars]] in his book 'Histoire des plantes du Dauphiné' Vol.3 on page 335 in 1786.<ref name="Plantlist" /><ref name="ipni">{{cite web|title=Ranunculaceae Ranunculus trichophyllus Chaix|url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do?id=30048831-2|publisher=ipni.org|access-date=27 October 2017}}</ref>

The species [[epithet]] ''trichophyllus'' is [[Latin]] for 'hairy leaves'.<ref>Archibald William Smith {{google books|ahNMkgoNJ7IC|A Gardener's Handbook of Plant Names: Their Meanings and Origins|page=339}}</ref>

In North America it is also commonly known as the 'white water crow foot'.<ref>Elaine Nowick {{google books|STTRCQAAQBAJ|Historical Common Names of Great Plains Plants, with Scientific Names Index ...|page=365}}</ref> The [[Icelandic language|Icelandic]] name of this species is Lónasóley.<ref>{{cite web|title=elements: Ranunculus trichophyllus, thread-leaved water-crowfoot|url=http://www.iceland-nh.net/plants/data/Ranunculus-trichophyllus/ranunculus_trichophyllus.html|publisher=iceland-nh.net|access-date=27 October 2017}}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
The plant is found in most of the Northern Hemisphere,<ref name="RHS" /> from the [[United States]], [[Europe]] and the [[Mediterranean]], east through [[Siberia]], the [[Caucasus]], the Middle East, the [[Himalayas]], [[Kazakhstan]] and [[Mongolia]] to [[Kamchatka]] in [[Russia]], also in [[Japan]], [[China]] and [[Korea]].<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />
It is even found in the lakes and ponds of [[Mount Everest]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Lacoul|first1=P.|last2=Freedman|first2=B.|title=Recent Observation of a Proliferation of Ranunculus trichophyllus Chaix. in High-Altitude Lakes of the Mount Everest Region|journal=Arctic, Antarctic, and Alpine Research|date=August 2006|volume=38|issue=3|pages=394–398|doi=10.1657/1523-0430(2006)38[394:rooapo]2.0.co;2|doi-access=free}}</ref>

==Phytoremediation==
{{Short description|Species of flowering plant}}
[[Phytoremediation]] is a plant-based approach, which involves the use of plants to extract and remove elemental pollutants or lower their bioavailability in soil.<ref name=":0" /> Ranunculus trichophyllus, commonly known as the threadleaf crowfoot or Three-leaved Crowfoot, is a species of aquatic plant. It belongs to the buttercup family ([[Ranunculaceae]]). However, it's not a widely studied or economically significant plant, and information about its specific importance might be limited. Therefore, in terms of [[Phytoremediation]], there is limited information other than the species participates in phytofiltration. Phytofiltration is a type of [[phytoremediation]] of heavy metal-polluted soil. Phytofiltration is the use of plant roots ([[rhizofiltratio]])), shoots (caulofiltration), or seedlings (blastofiltration) to remove pollutants from contaminated surface waters or waste waters. During [[rhizofiltration]], heavy metals are either adsorbed onto the root surface or absorbed by the roots. Root exudates can change [[rhizosphere]] pH, which leads to the precipitation of heavy metals on plant roots, further minimizing the movement of heavy metals to underground water.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Yan |first1=An |last2=Wang |first2=Yamin |last3=Tan |first3=Swee Ngin |last4=Mohd Yusof |first4=Mohamed Lokman |last5=Ghosh |first5=Subhadip |last6=Chen |first6=Zhong |date=2020 |title=Phytoremediation: A Promising Approach for Revegetation of Heavy Metal-Polluted Land |journal=Frontiers in Plant Science |volume=11 |article-number=359 |doi=10.3389/fpls.2020.00359 |issn=1664-462X |doi-access=free |pmid=32425957 |pmc=7203417 |bibcode=2020FrPS...11..359Y }}</ref> Ranunculus trichophyllus is great in phytofiltration to deal with [[arsenic]] which is accumulated in aquatic plants and eliminated from water.<ref>Ungureanu G, Santos S, Boaventura R, Botelho C. Arsenic and antimony in water and wastewater: overview of removal techniques with special reference to latest advances in adsorption. Journal of environmental management. 2015 Mar 15;151:326-42.</ref>

==Range==
It grows in freshwater,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Dalla Vecchia|first1=F.|last2=Cuccato|first2=F.|last3=La Rocca|first3=N.|last4=Larcher|first4=W.|last5=Rascio|first5=N.|title=Endodermis-like Sheaths in the Submerged Freshwater Macrophyte Ranunculus trichophyllus Chaix |url=https://oup.silverchair-cdn.com/oup/backfile/Content_public/Journal/aob/83/1/10.1006_anbo.1998.0787/2/830093.pdf |journal=Annals of Botany|date=January 1999|volume=83|issue=1|pages=93–97|doi=10.1006/anbo.1998.0787|bibcode=1999AnBot..83...93D |doi-access=free}}</ref> found in dune slacks and drainage ditches to ponds, lakes, streams and slow-flowing rivers.
It can be found up to {{convert|3000|m|ft|abbr=on}} above sea level.<ref name="iucn status 12 November 2021" />
